tldr: The headline layer for this story is almost entirely a single crime-event frame: across all 14 buckets, every outlet's title reduces the Banga shooting to a death count plus 'school shooting' label, with no headline surfacing the gun-policy, legal, or health dimensions prominent in the bodies. The only notable deviation is Malay Mail's title, which is the sole headline to anchor the event in a serial pattern ('Third deadly campus attack since June'), while the Daily Mail uniquely inflates the toll and uses sensationalist 'gun rampage' language found nowhere else.

evidence.quote: Philippines school shooting leaves at least three dead
Philippine teen kills two students, then himself
16-year-old embarks in gun rampage in Philippines
Third deadly campus attack since June

single_outlet_findings.finding: Inflates the death toll to 'at least six dead and many more injured' against every other outlet's confirmed three; 'gun rampage' language appears in no other headline in the corpus.

Only headline to embed serial-pattern context ('Third deadly campus attack since June'), shifting the framing from isolated incident to recurring national threat — a contextualisation absent from all other titles.

bottom_line: On the homepage layer, this story reads as a straightforward crime event — students killed by a student gunman in the Philippines — with gun-policy, legal, and public-health angles visible only to readers who click through to the bodies.
